content.text: I measured index 35 (V-rich), which gave 9.4 µA. Next I'm checking the Cu-rich vanadate region.

input.verdict: Mildly supportive: MACE says Cu2V2O7 is essentially on the hull (0.006 eV/atom), so a Cu:V near 1:1 composition should form this known vanadate photoabsorber. The MEGNet gap of 0.54 eV is a known PBE-like underestimate; the experimental gap is about 2 eV, below the 3.2 eV illumination. Index 199 (Cu 0.44, Fe 0.11, V 0.45) is the closest candidate to this composition with low Fe.

content.text:
I've submitted **index 199** (Cu 0.44, Fe 0.11, V 0.45) as the best composition. It gave a photocurrent of **1.79×10⁻⁵ A**, the highest of the three measurements the budget allowed.

| Index | Cu / Fe / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | 0.16 / 0.16 / 0.68 | 9.4×10⁻⁶ |
| **199** | 0.44 / 0.11 / 0.45 | **1.79×10⁻⁵** |
| 98 | 0.53 / 0.12 / 0.35 | 4.8×10⁻⁶ |

- **Why this region:** photocurrent roughly doubled going from the V-rich index 35 to 199, then fell to about a quarter of that at the more Cu-rich index 98. The peak is near a 1:1 Cu:V ratio, which matches Cu₂V₂O₇. The MACE-MP-0 model puts that phase almost on the convex hull (0.006 eV/atom), so it should form readily at this composition.
- **Band-gap model:** MEGNet's gaps for Cu₂V₂O₇ (0.54 eV HSE, 0.39 eV GLLB) are well below the roughly 2 eV measured experimentally, so they didn't help separate candidates.
- **Last measurement:** the GP model suggested index 138, a V-richer composition near Cu 0.37. I measured 98 instead to follow the Cu trend, and it turned out worse. The peak is only located to within that gap, so 138 or a nearby low-Fe composition could beat 199.

**Limits of the search:**
- **Phase list not read:** it was too large to return, and I had no tool to read the saved file. I found the Cu₂V₂O₇ phase ID by guessing, so apart from that one phase I didn't check any other known phase against the candidates.
- **No XRD:** none of the 5 XRD measurements were used, so no measured phase identity supports the result.
- **Fe-rich compositions untested:** none of the three measured points had more than 0.16 Fe.

With 3 measurements across 297 candidates, index 199 is the best I found, not necessarily the best in the library.
